This review is coming from a Warband vet of 1000+ hours.

Singleplayer in this game is pretty fun but many mechanics are flawed or broken. See all the ways it can be completely cheesed by watching any number of youtube videos. Its near impossible to start and form your own kingdom because of all these flaws. If you want to be a vassal sure, its not bad but the second you break out on your own you are under attack on all sides and it becomes a slog of non-stop assaults until your kingdom breaks.

Multiplayer is the biggest disappointment. After 10 years and advice from those who put thousands of hours in warband they completely ignored us. This combat in multiplayer is incredibly clunky and rewards using cheap tactics to win (aka horse spam, archer spam). They all but removed the two most popular game modes siege and battle for north america.
---COMBAT--- Combat in multiplayer feels clunky and slow. attacks are delayed, blocks are delayed. It feels like my mouse has 1-2second lag on clicks and input for combat. There are tons of complaints on the forums about these issues and the Devs refuse to even answer a single question about it. If you are coming from warband just wait to see if they actually fix any of these issues before purchasing.

Good:
After many years in development the game engine has been vastly improved, running both smooth and stable on modern PCs. The graphics and ui have undergone a much needed modernization.
Bad:
Content has been neglected throughout the Early Access process. The game has added "More" in a haphazard and inefficient manner. There are "more" quest givers but none of them surpass the function of the Warband guild-master or village chief. There are "more" factions but still the same number of culture troop trees. There are "More" AI nobles but less ways to interact with them. There are a LOT of dialogue trees that are still empty.
Modding:
Conflicting signalling from the Dev team on modding. In theory this is the main reason for a custom engine and all the development time is being spent to make it versatile and moddable. In practice, the modding community had to make their own tools for managing compatibility and supporting moddability, Butterlib and Harmony. There is no guarantee that the game will live up to its promise of surpassing the module system of Warband.

Post Early Access: Yeah the game didn't get better.

Did you love Mount and Blade 1, Warband or any variation of original M&B? You'll love Mount and Blade 2 Bannerlord then.

M&B2 takes the unique and fun formula of the original and greatly expands it in almost every aspect. Smithing gear, fighting with gangs, running settlements greatly expanded, skills expanded and refined, battles up to 1000 soldiers at a time, extremely visually improved and performance is just as good as the first game. The only performance slow down I notice is during massive battles and that's also because I run the game maxed out but it still stays above a playable frame rate. 99% of the time, I get a solid 60+ frames per second.

It would take paragraphs to explain and review every element and aspect this game has and all the improving I've seen across the board even though the game is still in early access. Even in it's current state, it's less buggy than M&B 1 and looks 10 times better. This game is good enough to be a complete product and is better than many fully released games on the market. It's worth the $40 price tag and if you can get it on sale, all the more value.

Bannerlord is a pretty good game. It's not exactly well-polished, but the developers have been making steady progress on fixing bugs and implementing missing perks. In its current state, it's quite playable, but there are a fair number of balance issues, and some minor annoyances.

The game is also particularly difficult. Assuming the difficulty is set on realistic, which I believe to be the intended difficulty- You don't start out as a superhero that can 1-shot anyone. You're just some random scrub with a sword and a horse, and the horse is pretty shitty. Forming a kingdom is also extremely difficult, and is something you probably won't be doing on your first couple of runs.

Still, the wide variety of game mechanics gives many options for every play style. My current playthough involves roaming the land and butchering large amounts of horses for a profit.

Bannerlord is hard to review. At the start of the sandbox, you are given a timed world quest to do to introduce you to lore, and give you an objective to work on.

Early game, you are killing bandits, going to arena fights, and smithing. You are constantly doing things to keep you engaged.
Mid game, when you decide to either join a faction or really start your own, your ability to play the game goes up and down. If you are at war, you can have 100 things to do at once. If you are at peace, you are, literally, sitting down and staring at timers go up or down.
Experience seems easy enough early, but then you read you need to get tens of millions of EXP to level up to those sweet looking end game perks... and each *manual* battle may give you 200 if you are lucky.
End game is, you guessed it, macro level, hands off gameplay. You don't GET to lead battles, because its more efficient to set timers up and watch NPCs go around and fight for you, because guess what, THEY are maxed level fighters with amazing perks that the player character will never experience without cheating or mods.

Honestly, its worth playing though your first time, and mods help, but at its core its JUST more M&B 1.
